identifiability.what_is_supported: Geometry can bind a virtual reference to a stable adjacent physical endpoint without moving q or testing centre material. Actual RGB can then be inspected for that endpoint; six background-centred queries still contain nearby structural corners.
identifiability.what_is_not_proved: The forward inputs do not explicitly name the expected part/endpoint. AUX0 contains visible wood belonging to a different target part; material or any-visible-corner supervision can reverse the intended target. Unique GT geometric association does not itself make the hidden endpoint identity observable.
identifiability.same_input_conflicts: The8 frozen q coordinates are distinct, so this small fixed set has no demonstrated strict identical-input contradictory label. A hidden switch of expected part at the same RGB/q would change the target without changing forward input; keep one fixed available association convention and preserve unresolved competition asU. This is a limitation, not proof that a fixed convention cannot be learned.
identifiability.S_E: A missing endpoint alone does not identify same-target self occlusion versus a foreign occluder. That separation needs target/foreign geometry ownership in the teacher and a declared expected-cue contract; crop-only causal identifiability remains empirical.
identifiability.boundary_U: Mixed incident-face probes, thin/ambiguous projected edges, ownership ties, partial or out-of-crop support must retain explicitU until the cue observability rule is fixed. Numerical U0 in36 rays is not semantic uncertainty0.
